title: An issue or PR's own timeline comment counts on a #N that isn't there
author: zashiki-warashi
description: Compares every ordinary issue/PR conversation comment's own body against the repository's own issue and PR sets: someone writes '#N' in ordinary prose inside the timeline discussion ('same root cause as #501', 'blocked on #N'), and no issue or PR numbered N exists in this repo. An eighth leg of the dangling-reference family alongside dangling-issue-reference (commit messages), mention-dangling-reference (X mentions), release-note-dangling-reference (release notes), issue-body-dangling-reference (issue/PR opening bodies), milestone-body-dangling-reference (milestone descriptions), own-tweet-dangling-reference (the town's own tweets), and review-comment-dangling-reference (a PR's own inline review comments) -- none of the seven ever read the ordinary timeline thread, the comments a human leaves on an issue or PR's own discussion, not anchored to any diff line.
confidence_notes: Age-gated off the comment's own updated_at, the identical shape review-comment-dangling-reference, issue-body-dangling-reference, and milestone-body-dangling-reference already established -- 0.55 within 24h since last update, 0.85 past it. Deliberately NOT flat, matching the editable-text-surface siblings rather than the permanent-text siblings: an ordinary comment, like a review comment, an issue/PR body, or a milestone description, is a text surface its author can edit at any time, so a fresh dangling reference earns a grace period before being scored as a confirmed gap. A reference that resolves against either the issue list or the PR list is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden. A cross-repo owner/repo#N reference is never even extracted as a candidate -- that names a different repo's own number space on purpose. A comment with no body at all is excluded outright -- there is no claim to have broken.
